relations.rationale: Jun's age has no bearing on whether the group quickened pace due to clouds.
Jun setting a pace for the group doesn't relate to how many teams existed.
Jun setting a steady pace is a separate cause from the clouds prompting a quicker pace, not directly related.
Esme and Eli being on different teams implies there are at least two teams, supporting the claim of two teams.
Stopping for lunch at midday doesn't determine whether clouds gathered later in the afternoon.
Reaching an outcrop for lunch is consistent with later reaching camp in the evening, supporting the timeline of progress.
Yara tracking time to reach camp before sunset is a different motivation than quickening due to clouds, but both push toward hastening, so it's largely unrelated in causal terms.
Clouds gathering directly caused the group to quicken their pace as stated.
Clouds gathering in the afternoon is consistent with the group later settling into camp in the evening.
Quickening pace toward the campsite supports the group successfully settling into camp by evening.
Settling into tents in the evening is consistent with being tired but satisfied with the day's progress.
Having settled into tents suggests the group is now ready to rest before continuing the next day.
Being tired but satisfied naturally leads to being ready to rest before the next leg.
